119f2913baa2dfaf6a8fd551066ef6844ec1c9a1.text: {"verdict":"accept","reasons":["The module implements what the card asks: a trend direction taken from the sign of the lookback return, with position size set by target_vol over annualized realized volatility and capped at max_leverage.","It is not a renamed copy of ts_momentum. It adds volatility-targeted sizing in place of a fixed unit count.","The template description matches the code, including the long_only flat behaviour, the whole-unit floor and the leverage cap.","The parameter bounds are sensible, and there are no hard-coded dates, prices or dataset-specific constants.","All static and conformance checks passed, including lookahead and determinism."],"criteria":[{"id":"c_signal","satisfied":true,"finding":"Direction is computed from price / closes[-1 - lookback] - 1. It is +1 if positive, -1 if negative and 0 if zero, and it is clamped to 0 for shorts when long_only is set. This is the sign of the return over the lookback window."},{"id":"c_sizing","satisfied":true,"finding":"Realized volatility is the sample std (ddof=1) of the last vol_window log returns, annualized with sqrt(252). Leverage is target_vol / annual_vol, capped at max_leverage. The target position is floor(leverage * equity / price) units. Size is therefore inversely proportional to recent realized volatility and aims at the target volatility. When volatility is zero, leverage falls back to the cap, which is a reasonable edge case."},{"id":"c_params","satisfied":true,"finding":"Three bounded parameters are exposed: lookback (integer, 5–250, default 60), vol_window (integer, 5–250, default 20) and target_vol (number, 0.01–1.0, default 0.1). The extra max_leverage (0.1–5.0) and long_only parameters are reasonable additions. The bounds_run check passed at 10 parameter sets."}]}

320cfcd8382cad71bbd4246864fb30878de6a161.text: {"verdict":"accept","reasons":["The module implements a genuine z-score mean-reversion signal: it fades closes that sit far from their rolling mean and exits when the close returns through the mean. It uses the sample std (ddof=1) over the last `lookback` closes, goes long at z <= -entry_z, goes short (or flat when long_only) at z >= entry_z, and exits on crossing the mean.","Lookback (integer, 5..250, default 20) and entry_z (number, 0.5..5.0, default 2.0) are exposed with sensible bounds.","Nothing is hard-coded to a dataset (no dates, prices or symbols). All static and conformance checks passed, including lookahead and determinism."],"criteria":[{"id":"c_signal","satisfied":true,"finding":"on_bar computes z = (last close - rolling mean) / rolling sample std over the last `lookback` closes. It buys `units` when z <= -entry_z and sells (short or flat) when z >= entry_z, so it fades deviations from the rolling mean. It flattens longs once z >= 0 and shorts once z <= 0. Zero or non-finite std is guarded."},{"id":"c_params","satisfied":true,"finding":"TEMPLATE exposes lookback as Param('integer', 5, 250, 20) and entry_z as Param('number', 0.5, 5.0, 2.0). Both are bounded with reasonable ranges for a rolling-window z-score strategy, and both are wired into the strategy constructor and used in the signal."}]}

6c5ac114cd859f4df460642681306a2752a00bce.text:
{"escalate":"No template written. The card can't be met under the current template interface without guessing about the pair, so this needs a human decision.

The card asks for a strategy that trades the spread between two named legs (criterion c_pair: long one symbol, short the other). The interface doesn't allow that:
- __init__ takes a single `symbol`.
- Param types are limited to integer, number and boolean, so the second leg can't be a parameter.
- I can't change the interface or any other file.

The only workaround is to infer the partner from whatever other symbols happen to appear in context.history, for example "the other symbol" or "the most correlated one". That would put a hidden, data-dependent choice of the second leg into the template. It would break or change meaning on datasets with more than two symbols. The pair would never be stated anywhere a reviewer or the human merging this could check. I didn't do that.

To proceed, the template interface needs a way to bind two symbols: a second symbol argument, a string or symbol Param type, or a host-level pair binding. Alternatively, the card owner could rescope the task to a single-symbol strategy. I can't make either change.","rationale":"Criterion c_pair needs two declared legs. The interface can declare only one symbol and has no string parameter, so the second leg could only be guessed from the dataset. Hiding that guess in a template would mislead the reviewer and could misbehave on other datasets, so I'm escalating rather than submitting a module."}

8c3c0119acf4545ac280e5d96c3948b97dfa9a4c.text: {"verdict":"accept","reasons":["The module implements a genuine channel breakout. The channel is the max and min of the previous `lookback` closes, taken as closes.iloc[-(n+1):-1], so the current bar is excluded. The latest close is compared against that channel. It is not a renamed copy of the existing ts_momentum template, which uses a return-sign signal.","The template description matches the code: +units above the upper channel, -units (or flat when long_only) below the lower channel, and no order otherwise, so the position is kept.","The channel length `lookback` is an integer parameter bounded 2–250 with default 20, which is sensible for a breakout channel.","The code has no hard-coded dates, prices or dataset-specific constants. All static and conformance checks passed, including lookahead and determinism."],"criteria":[{"id":"c_signal","satisfied":true,"finding":"on_bar builds the window from the previous N closes, excluding the current bar. It sets target=+units when the last close is above the window max. When the last close is below the window min, it sets target=-units, or 0 if long_only. Otherwise it returns no orders, so the position is held. This matches 'long above highest close of previous N bars, flat or short below lowest close of previous N bars'."},{"id":"c_params","satisfied":true,"finding":"The channel length is exposed as `lookback`, Param('integer', 2, 250, 20). It is bounded with a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 250, and the bounds_run check exercised 6 parameter sets successfully."}]}
